statements.claim: Mathura had thrown back the armies of Magadha; Jarasandha had come against the city once and then again, and the brothers scattered his forces with their own hands.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: Yadavas counsel that Mathura 'cannot withstand Jarasandha's repeated sieges'; Harivamsha 1.94 excerpt on the city's weakness presupposes prior repulses; two sieges established in the arc chain.

statements.claim: Vikadru rose in council and was counted the foremost speaker of the clan.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 (in pack): 'Vikadru, the foremost of royal speakers'.

statements.claim: Vikadru said Mathura cannot withstand another siege: the city has a limited supply of food and fuels, is not protected by a fort, and cannot stand attack for even one day.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.94 excerpt: 'This city has a limited supply of food and fuels. It is not protected by a fort... It will not therefore be able to stand attack for even one day.'

statements.claim: Someone protested that the brothers had beaten Jarasandha twice; Vikadru answered that a siege is answered with grain and stone, not in the field, and Jarasandha need only wait for hunger to do his work.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the 1.94 excerpt (thin stores, no walls, cannot stand one day) and the two prior sieges in the arc; the elaboration of how the siege would work is faithful connective reasoning on the pack's claims.

statements.claim: Mathura was a city of cowherds and traders, grown rich on the river and the pastures, never turned into a stronghold.
statements.evidence: Generic characterization consistent with the city's depiction in the tradition and the pack's 'city of cowherds' framing; not a sourceable discrete fact in the pack.

statements.claim: The council ended with the truth spoken and no decision made; that night Krishna stood at a window looking south toward the mountains where the answers might be waiting.
statements.evidence: Atmosphere/transitional narration setting up the following story; no factual assertion requiring support.

notes: All substantive claims map directly to Harivamsha 1.94-1.95. No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Vasudeva rose after the council and gave Vikadru's counsel his full assent, telling Krishna to do what he had said.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95: 'what the intelligent Vikadru, the foremost of royal speakers... has said, is true and well meaning... Do what that foremost of Yadus has said.'

statements.claim: Krishna's lesson in statecraft: a king daily meditates on peace and war, on alliance and dissension; the learned king does not place himself before a powerful enemy but withdraws, and in proper time and according to his strength engages in battle again.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 v.6-8: 'A king daily meditates on peace, quarrel... A learned king should not place himself before a powerful enemy, but rather should fly away. And in proper time and according to his strength he should engage in fight.'

statements.claim: Krishna said: 'Therefore, although I am capable, I shall, at this very moment, fly away with the worshipful Baladeva — like one incapable, saving my life.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 v.9 and pack excerpt: 'Therefore although I am capable, I shall, at this very moment, fly away with the worshipful Baladeva for saving my life like one incapable.'

statements.claim: The plan: go south, ascend mount Sahya, enter the Deccan, see the charming cities of Karavira and Krouncha and the foremost of mountains Gomanta.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 v.10-11: 'Ascending the mount Sahya... I shall enter into Deccan and we shall behold the charming cities of Karavira and Krounch and the foremost of mountains Gomanta.'

statements.claim: Krishna said Jarasandha, elated with success, would not sit before Mathura but pursue them in pride into the forests of Sahya, and that the departure is conducive to the well-being of the race of Yadu; the province, city and citizens will fare well.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 v.12-14: 'that Emperor, elated with success, will not enter into this city but rather will pursue us in pride... this our departure is conducive to the well-being of the race of Yadu. By this, the Province, the city and the citizens will fare well.'

statements.claim: That very day the two brothers set out for the south without the least anxiety, taking on different forms at will and traveling through hundreds of kingdoms.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95: 'set out for the south without experiencing the least anxiety in mind'; 'Assuming forms at will they began to travel in hundreds of southern kingdoms.'

statements.claim: Long ago, in the time of king Yadu, his five sons went out to found cities: Padmavarna raised Karavira on mount Sahya, and Sarasas laid out Krouncha in its groves; the brothers came at last to Karavira, presided over by members of their own family.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 v.19: 'reached the city of Karavira, presided over by the members of their own family and adorned with the mount Sahya'; founding names from Harivamsha 1.94 (in pack for DKS_0151): 'The royal saint Padmavarna laid out, on the mountain Sahya... his city was known by the name of Karavira' and 'Sārasa built his highly charming city Krouncha.'

statements.claim: On the bank of the river Vena stood a great fig tree, and under its shade the two brothers paused to rest.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 v.19-20: 'They saw there a huge fig tree on the bank of the river Venā.'

statements.claim: The appearance of the flight as fear was a weapon: this flight would read as the retreat of a beaten man.
statements.evidence: Interpretive framing of Krishna's 'like one incapable' phrasing; non-factual commentary on the source's own words.

notes: Quotes match Harivamsha 1.95 closely. The five-sons founding detail draws on Harivamsha 1.94, present in the corpus evidence (pack of DKS_0151). No issues.

statements.claim: On the bank of the river Vena under a great fig tree sat an old ascetic milking a cow white as the milky arani tree, her calf beside her, giving milk whenever wished.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95: 'milching his sacrificial cow with her calf ever giving milk whenever desired and white as the milky Arani tree... He was seated at the foot of that tree, had his axe on his shoulder, wore bark and matted locks, was white as the flames of fire... was emaciated with the performance of three oblations a day.'

statements.claim: Krishna recognized him as Rama, son of Jamadagni, born in the race of Bhrigu, the destroyer of the Kshatriyas.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 v.28: 'Rāma, the son of Jamadagni born in the race of Bhrigu, and the destroyer of the Kshatriyas.'

statements.claim: Parasurama had agitated the ocean with the speed of his shafts and laid out the city of Surpara on its shore.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95: 'having agitated the ocean with the velocity of thy shafts thou hast laid out a city by name Surpāra.'

statements.claim: Remembering his slain father, he went out with his axe and cut down the thousand arms of Kartavirya like a forest.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95: 'Remembering the destruction of thy sire thou didst, with thy axe, chop off the thousand arms of Kārtavirya resembling a forest.'

statements.claim: The earth's mud was still said to be stained with the blood of the warrior kings he had slain.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95: 'Even now the Earth has her mud covered with the cool blood of the Kshatryas who were killed by thy axe.'

statements.claim: Krishna identified himself and Balarama as the two Yadavas living on the bank of the Yamuna, telling their story: placed in Vraja by Vasudeva out of fear of Kamsa, grew up without fear, came of age, destroyed Kamsa in the assembly, set Ugrasena back on the royal seat, returned to cowherd work, then Jarasandha besieged the city repeatedly until they left to draw him away.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95 v.29-39: 'perhaps thou mightest have heard of two Yādavas living on the bank of the Yamunā. We are those two... our father Vasuveda... afraid of Kansa, placed us in Vraja... we grew up without any fear... we entered into Mathurā and powerfully destroyed the haughty Kansa in the assembly... placing his father Ugrasena in his royal office we again... engaged in the work of cow-herd boys... thereafter when Jarāsandha laid seige to our c[ity]...'

statements.claim: Parasurama counseled: get up onto that high summit; if you obstruct Jarasandha by fighting with him from the fort there, you will be able to conquer him.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Getting upon that high summit... if you obstruct Jarasandha by fighting with him in the fort you will be able to conquer him.'

statements.claim: So the mountain was named: Gomanta.
statements.evidence: The name Gomanta is already given in Krishna's own plan (1.95 v.10-11); the sentence is a connective pointer to the mountain in question rather than a claim that the name originated from this counsel.

statements.claim: The brothers stayed a while with the sage on the bank of the Vena, then turned their faces toward Gomanta.
statements.evidence: Follows from the 1.95 sequence: the meeting by the Vena, the counsel, and the subsequent journey to Gomanta (per the arc chain; next title 'Krishna Wields the Divine Weapons on Gomanta').

statements.claim: The old sage sat quiet as the preceptor of the gods, still as the ocean.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.95: 'motionless like the ocean... was like the very preceptor of gods.'

notes: All descriptions and the counsel map to Harivamsha 1.95. 'So the mountain was named: Gomanta' read as connective narration since Gomanta was already named earlier in the same chapter. No issues.

statements.claim: The kings' soldiers saw the two brothers coming down from the mountain with no weapon but their arms, moving like two makaras that agitate the ocean, and terror ran through the host.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.1-2: 'Beholding the two sons of Vasudeva come down from the mountain the soldiers of the kings grew terrified... Although they had no other weapons but their arms they began to move about there in anger like two Makaras that agitate the ocean.'

statements.claim: The weapons the brothers had obtained before in their encounter at Mathura came down from the sky like burning flames before the assembled kings — huge bodily weapons adorned with celestial garlands, lighting up the ten quarters, as if thirsting for battle.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.3-8: 'The weapons, which they had obtained before in their encounter at Mathura, came down from the sky like burning flames... adorned with celestial garlands, lighted up the ten quarters with their lustre.' (Source: 'filled with thirst and the desire of feeding upon human flesh'; story's 'thirsting for battle' is a softened but faithful rendering of 'thirst'.)

statements.claim: Four Vaishnava weapons came down: the plough-share Samvartaka, the mace Saunanda, the discus Sudarshana, and the club Koumodaki.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'came down for the two Yadavas four powerful Vaishnava weapons namely, the plough-share Samvartaka, the mace Sounanda, the discus Sudarshana, and the club Koumodaki.'

statements.claim: Balarama, foremost of the Satvatas, took the plough-share in his left hand and the mace Saunanda in his right; Krishna took the discus Sudarshana and the club Koumodaki.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.9-14: 'the powerful Rāma, the foremost of Sātwatas... took up with his left hand the plough-share... and with his right hand, the best of maces Saunanda... Keshava... took up the discus Sudarshana... The other hand of Krishna... was bedecked with the club Koumodaki.'

statements.claim: The two brothers were one in Vishnu, divided into two for the sake of men.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.16-17: 'although one in Vishnu, divided into two as men under the names of Rāma and Govinda.'

statements.claim: Balarama dragged the cars of the Kshatriyas from their courses, venting his anger on horses and elephants, churning mountain-like elephants with his mace.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.18-20: 'dragging the cars of the highly powerful Kshatriyas he began to give effect to his anger on the horses and the elephants... assailing with the strokes of his mace mountain-like elephants... he began as if to churn them.'

statements.claim: The leading Kshatriyas, on the point of being slain, abandoned their cars in fear and fled to Jarasandha.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.21-22: 'the leading Kshatriyas, who were on the point of being slain by Rāma, left their cars in fear, and went to Jarāsandha.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha rebuked them: 'Fie on your conduct as Kshatriyas grown tired of battle'; those who fly leaving their cars behind are visited by the sin of destroying an embryo; 'Why do you flee in fear of a milk-herd of limited power who fights on foot?'; he vowed to despatch the two cowherd boys to the abode of Yama.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.22-25, quoted nearly verbatim in the story.

statements.claim: Rallied, the Kshatriyas returned with a downpour of arrows — coats of mail, swords, quivers, horses with golden reins, cars of moon-like lustre, cloud-like elephants — and the kings shone under rising umbrellas and chowries.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.26-29: 'engaged in fight with a downpour of arrows. With coats of mail, Nishtringsas, weapons, quivers... horses adorned with golden reins, cars of moon-like lustre and cloud-like elephants... Covered with rising umbrellas and fanned with beautiful chowries the kings... shone greatly in beauty.'

statements.claim: Thousands of arrows shot by the kings struck the two descendants of the Yadu race, and they bore them like mountains sprinkled with rain; assailed by heavy clubs and maces they did not tremble.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.32-33: 'Those two heroic descendants of the Yadu race bore thousands of arrows shot by the kings like two mountains sprinkled with rain. Although assailed by heavy clubs and maces they did not tremble.'

statements.claim: Krishna, like a cloud swollen with wind, increased his body and with the discus cut down men, horses, elephants and mighty car-warriors.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.34-35: 'Krishna, resembling a cloud... increased his body like a cloud accompanied by wind. And with his discus effulgent like the sun he began to cut down men, horses, elephants and mighty car-warriors.'

statements.claim: Balarama dragged the kings with his plough-share and struck them with his club until they lost consciousness; the variegated chariots broke down, their car-wheels obstructed.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.36-37: 'Rāma too so dragged the kings with his plough share and so struck them with his club, that they... could not stand... The car-wheels being obstructed the variegated chariots of the kings were broken down.'

statements.claim: In the thick of the slaughter, king Darada fell before Balarama.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'Balarama slays king Darada'; story content_note: 'includes the slaying of king Darada' (passage excerpt cuts before this verse but the pack's own summary asserts it).

statements.claim: Jarasandha was still beyond the broken ranks, and the brothers knew he would come again.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the 1.99 outcome and the arc chain (next story opens with Jarasandha having fled but the war continuing; Jarasandha's enmity is the arc's driving thread).

notes: Battle narrative maps almost verbatim to Harivamsha 1.99. 'As if thirsting for battle' softens the source's 'thirst... for human flesh' but preserves the source's own 'thirst' image; acceptable. No issues.

statements.claim: Jarasandha himself had fled when the battle turned; the alliance that had besieged Gomanta scattered and the mountain stood.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'After Jarasandha flees, the king of Chedi... befriends him'; Harivamsha 1.99 passage on the rout of the kings.

statements.claim: It was Jarasandha who had rallied the faltering Kshatriyas with bitter words — fie on their conduct, fleeing from a milk-herd who fought on foot — and his fury had held the line for a while; the kings came back in a downpour of arrows and the brothers stood under it like two mountains sprinkled with rain.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.99 v.22-33: Jarasandha's rebuke, the rallied Kshatriyas' downpour of arrows, and the brothers 'bore thousands of arrows... like two mountains sprinkled with rain.'

statements.claim: The king of Magadha, who had bound a dozen kings into his siege and sworn he would despatch the two cowherd boys to the abode of Yama, had ridden away with the rest when the battle turned.
statements.evidence: The pack supports Jarasandha's vow to despatch the brothers to Yama (1.99 v.25) and the gathering of kings against Gomanta ('the assembled kings'), but nowhere states the number of kings as 'a dozen'; the specific count is invented.

statements.claim: The king of Chedi, remembered by the Yadavas as kin for his house was bound to theirs by marriage, rode forward alone after the battle and stopped at a courteous distance.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'the highly effulgent king of Chedi, remembering his relationship with the Yadavas, approached Krishna'; pack summary: 'Krishna's kinsman by marriage.'

statements.claim: He said: this war was never mine by choice; I have seen what your arms can do; let us go together, my army and my followers and I, to the city of Karavira.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Let us go with our army and followers to the city of Karavira'; the framing of kinship and renunciation of the war elaborates the source's 'remembering his relationship with the Yadavas'.

statements.claim: Krishna accepted him at once; Balarama stood by without objection, and they set out the same day, the small army of the Chedi king and the two sons of Vasudeva riding together.
statements.evidence: Implied by the pack summary ('befriends him and escorts him to the city of Karavira') and by the outcome in the following episode (DKS_0156 opens with the column arriving at Karavira).

statements.claim: The country people who had hidden during the siege came to the roadside as the column passed, and the word ran ahead: the war is over, and the king of Chedi rides with Krishna; no plunder and no tribute, only a kinsman's word.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric scene-setting with no sourceable factual assertion; consistent with a peaceful allied journey to Karavira.

statements.claim: The king of Chedi was a man of years who looked almost young again with the fear of the field gone from his eyes.
statements.evidence: Generic descriptive coloring not asserted as a sourceable fact in the pack.

corrections.original_sentence: The king of Magadha, who had bound a dozen kings into his siege and sworn he would despatch the two cowherd boys to the abode of Yama, had ridden away with the rest when the battle turned.
corrections.suggested: The king of Magadha, who had bound the kings into his siege and sworn he would despatch the two cowherd boys to the abode of Yama, had ridden away with the rest when the battle turned.

notes: One UNSUPPORTED numeric detail: 'a dozen kings' (the pack gives no count of the besieging kings). Everything else maps to Harivamsha 1.99 and the pack summary.

statements.claim: King Shrigala drove out of Karavira to meet the arriving column on a chariot that shone like the car of Indra, with quick-coursing horses, golden axles and inexhaustible quivers, and the earth sank a little under its weight.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.1-11: 'Mounting a car filled with weapons... drawn by quick-coursing horses, embellished with strong golden axles... resembling the car of Indra... Stricken with fear... the Earth sank under his weight.'

statements.claim: He had heard how the armies of the kings had fared on Mount Gomanta, and the report offended him.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.17-18: 'I have heard of thy work in the weak army of the stupid kings on the mount Gomanta who had no leader... the defeat of the useless Kshatriyas.'

statements.claim: Shrigala challenged Krishna: 'I am the emperor of the world. You are alone, and I am with my army, so I should not fight you with all these men. Come, I will fight you alone, and one of us will meet his death in a fair fight. If you are slain, I shall be the only Vasudeva in the world. And if I am slain, you shall be the only one.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.19-22: 'I am now stationed in the dignity of the emperor of the world... Thou art alone and I am with my army; so I should not fight with thee in this way. Come, I shall alone fight with thee... one of us will meet with his death in a fair fight... If thou art slain... I shall be the only Vāsudeva in the world. And if I am slain thou shalt be the only one.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered: 'Strike me as you wish.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.23: 'saying "Strike me as you wish" the forgiving Mādhava held up his discus.'

statements.claim: Shrigala discharged a net of arrows, showering Krishna with shafts, maces and weapons covered with flame; Krishna stood motionless like a mountain.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.24-26: 'discharged a net of arrows at Krishna... showered on Krishna mace and various other weapons. And albeit ruthlessly assailed with weapons covered with flames of fire Krishna stood there motionless like a mountain.'

statements.claim: Krishna hurled the discus that had come to him at Gomanta; it struck Shrigala in the breast, pierced him through, and returned to Krishna's hand; Shrigala fell from his chariot like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt, bleeding.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.27-29: 'he hurled it at Shrigala's breast... the discus Sudarshana returned to its preceptor's hand. Shrigala too, having his heart pierced by the discus... fell down, bleeding like a cleft mountain... fallen like a mountain struck down by a thunder-bolt.'

statements.claim: His army broke: some fled, some entered the city weeping, some stood bewailing their fallen king.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.30-32: 'his soldiers lost heart and fled away... Some... entered into the city and began to weep... Some, not being able to forsake their fallen king... began to bewail there.'

statements.claim: Krishna declared safety to the people and said 'Do not fear! Do not fear' in a voice like the rumbling of clouds.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.33-34: 'declaring safety unto the people... Krishna... said with a voice like the rumbling of clouds. "Do not fear! Do not fear."'

statements.claim: The ministers and citizens wept, and the queens came out of the city with their sons, striking their breasts and crying over the fallen king.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.100 v.35-40: 'Shrigāla's subjects and ministers began to shed tears... Shrigāla's queens, with their sons, came out weeping from the city... striking their breasts with their hands, began to weep plaintively.'

statements.claim: The queen Padmavati came with her son, the boy prince Shakradeva, and pleaded for her son; Krishna said 'This son of Shrigala is as my own. I declare safety to you all.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'this son of Shrigala is just like mine. I declare safety unto them and gladly annoint him as the king'; pack summary: 'At the plea of Shrigala's queen, Krishna installs the slain king's son Shakradeva on the throne of Karavira' (characters Padmavati, Shakradeva).

statements.claim: Krishna lifted the prince onto the throne of Karavira, sprinkled him with celestial water, and anointed him king.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Placing the prince on the throne the powerful Janarddana sprinkled him with celestial water'; 'gladly annoint him as the king.'

statements.claim: The gates of Karavira opened before the column had even reached them, and the king came out as a storm comes out of a clear sky.
statements.evidence: Scene-setting for Shrigala's sortie; the source has him issue out upon being informed of their arrival — consistent, presented with imagery.

notes: Nearly every sentence tracks Harivamsha 1.100. The queen's name Padmavati and prince Shakradeva are taken from the pack's index/summary. No issues.

statements.claim: The kings of the earth gathered in the golden assembly hall of Bhishmaka at Kundina for the swayamvara of his daughter; when Krishna arrived with Garuda and the Yadavas, the leading kings were stricken with anxiety and fell silent.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.1-3: 'Beholding the eternal Krishna arrive there with Vināta's son the leading kings were stricken with great anxiety... assembled at the golden assembly hall of king Bhismaka.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha warned that Krishna, the well-known son of Vasudeva endued with great energy and prowess, has come for the maiden and will set forth mighty exertions to win her; the kings should behave according to the rules of polity, weighing their own strength and weakness.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.6-8: 'This Krishna, the well known son of Vasudeva... is endued with great energy and prowess. He has come here for the maiden and forsooth he will set forth mighty exertions for acquiring her... you should behave... according to the rules of Polity... considering your own strength and weakness.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha recalled what the two sons of Vasudeva did on Mount Gomanta without Garuda's help, and said that when Vishnu sits on Garuda and sets forth his exertions for the maiden, even Indra assisted by all the celestials will not be able to stand in the battle-field.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.9-11: 'You know well the highly dreadful work which these two powerful sons of Vasudeva performed on the mount Gomanta without the help of Vinatā's son... When seated on Garuda Vishnu will set forth his exertions for acquiring the maiden, even Sakra, assisted by the celestials... will not be able to stand in the battle-field.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha recited Krishna's previous deeds: boar form raised the drowned earth and killed Hiranyaksha; man-lion form slew Hiranyakashipu, who could not be killed in the three worlds, sky, earth or nether region, in day or night, by anything dry or wet; dwarf form bound Bali with a noose of promise and sent him to the nether region.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.12-16: boar form 'released the earth... killed Hiranyaksha the king of Daityas'; 'Hiranyakashipu, who did not meet with his death in the three worlds... in the sky, on the earth, and in the nether region, in day or in night, from a dry or an wet article, was slain... by Hari in his man-lion form'; 'Binding the powerful Bali... with a noose of promise Vishnu, in his form of a dwarf, sent him down to the nether region.'

statements.claim: At the junction of the ages he took birth in disguise from Jamadagni and Renuka as Rama with the axe and cut down the thousand-armed Kartavirya, elated with the pride of his kingdom.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.17-20: 'the highly powerful king Kārtavirya, endued with thousand arms, grew elated with the pride of kingdom... Vishnu took his birth in disguise, from Jamadagni and Renukā, as Rāma... and killed him with his axe.'

statements.claim: He was Dasharatha's son Rama, born in the race of Ikshvaku, who killed Ravana, the conqueror of the three worlds; in the Taraka-rooted war, eight-armed and seated on Garuda, he killed the boon-elated Asuras, and with his sun-effulgent discus killed the demon Kalanemi who terrorized the gods.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.21-24: 'Dasharatha's son Rāma, born in the race of Ikshāku... killed the heroic Rāvana, the conqueror of the three worlds'; 'In the Tretā age in the war of which Tāraka was the root, the powerful Vishnu, seated on Garuda, assuming a form of eight arms, killed... the Asuras... killed, with his discus, effulgent like the sun, the demon Kālanemi who terrorized the gods.'

statements.claim: As a boy in the forest he slew the demons Dhenuka, Arishta and Pralamba; in his cowherd form Devaki's son slew Putana, Keshi, the elephant Kuvalayapida, the wrestlers Chanura and Mushtika, and Kamsa with all his followers.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.25-28: 'as a boy in the forest, many... demons, Dhenuka, Arishtha and Pralamva have been slain. Slaying in his cow-herd form Shakuni, Putanā, Keshi, Jamala, Arjuna, the elephant Kuvalayapida, Chānura, Mushitika and Kansa with his followers Devaki's son sported there.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha declared his sure understanding, acquired at Mathura, that Devaki's son Keshava is the first cause of the celestials, the destroyer of the Asuras, Narayana, the ancient Purusha, the prime cause of the universe, Truth, the creator of all creatures manifest and unmanifest, unconquerable, unborn, eternal, the lord of the three worlds.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.29-33: 'I consider Devaki's son Keshava as the first cause of the celestials, the destroyer of the Asuras, as Nārāyana, the ancient Purusha, the Prime cause of the universe, as Truth, the creator of all creatures manifest and unmanifest... unconquerable... unborn... the lord of the three worlds... This my sure under standing, I have acquired from Mathurā.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha concluded: can Garuda be the carrier of a mere man, even a mortal lord paramount? When Janarddana displays his prowess for the maiden, what powerful man will stand before Garuda? Vishnu himself has come for this swayamvara; mighty is the calamity that will befall you on his arrival; do whatever you think proper.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105 v.34-36: 'Can Garuda be the carrier of a man even if he be born in the high family of a mortal Lord Paramount? Besides when Janarddana will display his prowess for the maiden what powerful man will be able to stand before Garuda? Forsooth I tell you that Vishnu himself has come for this Swayamvara. Mighty is the calamity that will befall you on his arrival here.'

statements.claim: Sunitha rose and gave his voice to the king of Magadha's words, and the kings knew the warning would not be argued away.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.105: 'After Jarāshandha... the greatly wise Sunitha replied saying...'; and 1.106 (in pack for DKS_0158): Dantavakra refers to 'what the king of Magadha and Sunitha have said for our well-being' — confirming Sunitha concurred with Jarasandha.

notes: Jarasandha's speech is a near-verbatim rendering of Harivamsha 1.105. Sunitha's concurrence is confirmed by 1.106's opening in the next pack. No issues.

statements.claim: Dantavakra, the king of Karusha, rose and endorsed the warning: what the king of Magadha and Sunitha have said for our well-being appears proper; he could not blame these nectarine words out of malice, pride, or any desire for victory of his own.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.1-4: 'the heroic Dantavakra, the king of Karusha said... what the king of Magadha and Sunitha have said for our well-being appears to me as proper. I cannot blame these nectarine words out of malice, pride or of my own desire for victory.'

statements.claim: Dantavakra recalled the war: because of Kamsa's foolishness the two heroes first lived in Vrindavana; Kamsa invited Rama and Keshava and set an infuriated elephant against them; they slew the elephant, entered the arena, and slew Kamsa, king of Mathura, with his followers — what offence did they commit that we all, elderly in age, came to Mathura at another's instigation?
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.8-11: 'on account of Kansa's foolishness those two heroes first lived in Vrindāvana... Kansa invited Rāma and Keshava and set an infuriated elephant against them. Slaying that elephant those two heroes entered the arena... they slew Kansa, the king of Mathurā... with his followers. What offence did they commit thereby, that we all, elderly in age, came to Mathura at (another's) instigation.'

statements.claim: Dantavakra continued: terrified at our huge and overwhelming army, Rama and Keshava left their own city and soldiers and fled to Gomanta; we pursued them and were defeated by those two boys; we laid siege to the hill, as Kshatriyas should, and set fire to it; had they died quietly in that conflagration we would have considered them humbled; we blame Janarddana because he fought against us.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.12-15: 'terrified at our huge and overwhelming army, Rāma and Keshava, leaving their own city and soldiers, fled away to Gomanta. We still pursued them there; and though expert in the art of fighting we were defeated... we laid seige to the hill and set fire to it... if they had given up their life quietly in that conflagration considering it a forest fire we would have considered them humbled. We blame Janārddana because he fought against us.'

statements.claim: Dantavakra concluded: as matters stand, wherever we go we shall pick up a quarrel, so let us contract friendship with Krishna; Krishna has come for the maiden, not for a quarrel.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.16-17: 'wherever we shall go we will pick up a quarrel. Let us, therefore... contract friendship with Krishna... Krishna has not come to this city of Kundina for picking up a quarrel. He has come for the maiden.'

statements.claim: Dantavakra declared Krishna not an ordinary human being but the foremost of men in the land of mortals and the foremost of gods in the land of celestials, the Deity and Creator of the worlds; in God there is no malice, pride or crookedness; the gods do not grow stupified or lean, are not visited by calamity, and remove the calamities of those who bow unto them.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.18-19: 'Krishna is not an ordinary human being. He is the foremost of men in this land of mortals, the foremost of gods in the land of celestials. He is the Deity and the Creator of the worlds. In God there is no malice, pride or crookedness. They are not stupified, they do not grow lean and are not visited by any calamity. They always remove the calamities of those who bow unto them.'

statements.claim: Dantavakra said Vishnu, the king of gods, has come with Garuda to show his true form; Krishna never goes with his army to slay his enemies; his coming accompanied by the leading Bhojas, Vrishnis, Andhakas and Yadavas indicates his desire of contracting friendship; let us offer the high-souled Keshava hospitality with arghya and water to rinse his mouth, and if we make peace with Keshava we shall live freed from anxiety and fear.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.20-24, quoted nearly verbatim; also pack excerpt: 'let us go and offer the high-souled Keshava hospitality... if we make peace with Keshava we shall be able to live freed from anxiety and fear.'

statements.claim: Salwa, the foremost of speakers, rose and scorned the fear: had they trembled at Krishna and thought it proper to make peace, they would have left their weapons at that time; speaking ill of one's own army and extolling another is not the duty of Kshatriya kings; we are born in great royal families and have glorified our races; why should our sense be poor like a coward's?
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.25-28: 'Sālwa, the foremost of speakers, said... What is the use of this fear? Had we trembled in Krishna's fear and thought it proper to make peace with him, we would have left our weapons at that time... Such is not the duty of the Kshatriya kings. We are all born in great royal families and have glorified our respective races. Why should then our sense be poorly like that of a coward.'

statements.claim: Salwa declared he knows Devaki's son Krishna as the immortal, eternal Prime Deity Vishnu, invincible unto the kings, powerful, adored of all the worlds, Vaikuntha, the preceptor of the entire world; and knows all the objects of Vishnu: the destruction of king Kamsa, the relieving of the earth of her burden, our destruction, and the protection of the worlds.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.29-32: 'I know Devaki's son Krishna as the immortal, eternal, Prime Deity Vishnu, invincible unto the kings, powerful, adored of all the worlds, Vaikuntha and the preceptor of the entire world... I know full well all the objects of Vishnu. He has in view... the destruction of king Kansa, the relieving of the earth of her burden, our destruction and the protection of the worlds.'

statements.claim: Salwa said: a great battle will take place between Vishnu and all the kings; consumed by the fire of his discus we will go to the abode of Yama; yet no one meets with untimely death and no one survives when the proper time comes, so a man should not entertain fear.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.31-34: 'a great battle will take place between Vishnu and all the kings... consumed by the fire of his discus we will go to the abode of Yama. Still considering that no one meets with untimely death, no one survives when the proper time comes and the lease of his life runs out... therefore a man should not entertain fear.'

statements.claim: Salwa recalled that when the ascetic virtue of the Daityas is annihilated, Vishnu, conversant with yoga, brings about their destruction in due time; he sent down the mighty Bali to the nether region and has performed many other feats like this; do not question the subject of fighting.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.106 v.35-36: 'When the ascetic virtue of the Daityas is annihilated the Divine Vishnu, conversant with Yoga, brings about their destruction in proper time. This Lord of gods sent down Virochona's son, the highly powerful Bali, to the nether region... Vishnu has performed many other feats like this; you should not therefore question the subject of fighting.'

statements.claim: Through it all Bhishmaka, king of Kundina, host of the council and father of the maiden and of the arrogant young Rukmi, had listened in silence; rising from his seat, he resolved to go himself to Krishna to propitiate, before any war began, the suitor the whole earth had gathered to deny.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Bhismaka felt a desire to go to eternal Krishna for propitiating him'; pack summary: 'Bhishmaka, fearing for his arrogant son Rukmi, resolves to go and propitiate Krishna.'

statements.claim: The council still rang with argument behind Bhishmaka as he stepped out into the evening, and Kundina went on lighting its lamps.
statements.evidence: Transitional scene-setting closing the episode; no sourceable factual assertion.

notes: Both speeches track Harivamsha 1.106 closely, often near-verbatim. Bhishmaka's motivation (Rukmi) is drawn from the pack summary. No issues.
